summary: the file is not YAML the reader can follow (a tab in the indentation, a duplicate key, an alias with no anchor, a line outside the structure)
fix: Fix the line named, or keep the file to the YAML that configtx.yaml files use (docs/inputs.md).

summary: the file holds a YAML construct the reader passes over (a block scalar, a tag, a complex key, a second document, a quoted string over several lines); what it holds was not checked
fix: Write the value in the plain form, or check that part by hand.

summary: the file has no Profiles section with a profile in it, so there is no channel or consortium to check
fix: Add the profiles the network is built from, or give the file that holds them.

summary: the Application section of a profile, or a consortium, lists one organization
fix: List every organization that is to be a member, so that the policies have more than one party to agree.
own: the count of one is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Fabric documentation; the page says a channel is a way for organizations to communicate

summary: the Admins policy of the Application, Orderer or Channel section is ANY Admins, so the admins of any one organization can approve a change to that group
fix: Use MAJORITY Admins, as the sample file does, or a signature policy that names the organizations whose approval is required.

summary: a Readers or Writers policy of the Application, Orderer or Channel section is ANY, which lets any one organization read or submit
fix: Confirm that open reading and submitting is intended. The documentation defaults are ANY, and MAJORITY on Writers would need several organizations to sign every submission, so this is a note and not a fault.
own: treating ANY as worth a look is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Fabric documentation; the documentation defaults are ANY

summary: the LifecycleEndorsement or Endorsement policy of the Application section is ANY, so one organization can approve a chaincode definition or endorse a transaction
fix: Use MAJORITY Endorsement, as the sample file does, or a signature policy that names who must endorse.

summary: an organization used in the Application section of a profile has no AnchorPeers
fix: Give the organization AnchorPeers, or set its anchor peers in a channel update after the channel exists; the pages say at least one must be defined in the channel configuration.
own: the current sample file no longer lists AnchorPeers, so a file written for the current release may set them in a channel update instead; the check cannot see a later update

summary: the OrdererType of a profile is solo
fix: Use etcdraft, or BFT where the release supports it, with several ordering nodes.

summary: an etcdraft profile lists fewer than 3 consenters, or none
fix: List at least three consenters, each on its own host.
own: the threshold of three is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Fabric documentation; the documentation says a production network should use a multi-node ordering service

summary: a BFT profile lists fewer than 4 consenters in its ConsenterMapping
fix: List at least 3F+1 consenters for the F failures the network is to tolerate, so at least four.

summary: all the consenters of a profile are on one host
fix: Put each consenter on its own host, so that one failure cannot stop ordering.
own: the idea that consenters should not share a host is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Fabric documentation

summary: a consenter has no ClientTLSCert or no ServerTLSCert
fix: Give every consenter both certificate paths, as the Raft page shows.

summary: the Orderer section of a profile sets no BatchTimeout, or no BatchSize or one of its three values
fix: Set BatchTimeout and BatchSize with MaxMessageCount, AbsoluteMaxBytes and PreferredMaxBytes, as the sample file does.
own: the tool does not know the values configtxgen fills in when a setting is left out, because the pages it reads do not say, so it asks for them to be written

summary: a profile has no Capabilities for its Channel, Application or Orderer group
fix: Add Capabilities with the level the binaries of the network support, set to true.

summary: a Capabilities group of a profile has no level set to true (for example V2_0: false)
fix: Set the level the binaries of the network support to true.

summary: an organization has no ID or no MSPDir
fix: Give the organization its ID and the MSPDir of its MSP folder.

summary: two organization definitions have the same MSP ID
fix: Give every organization its own MSP ID; use one definition and an alias where the same organization is meant.
